resale_co.name: Continued Certificate of Occupancy (resale C.O.)
resale_co.issued_by: Borough of Pine Hill (town code names the Construction Official; the borough's Construction Office page sends resale C.O. requests to the Pine Hill Fire Department / Fire District)
resale_co.lead_time: Town code: inspection within five working days after the application and fee are received.
resale_co.valid_for: Town code: an application is valid for six months from filing; after that a new application and fee are needed.
requirements: Town code: the home must comply with state and borough building, plumbing, electrical, zoning, health, safety, fire and minimum housing standards (including the International Property Maintenance Code) before the certificate is issued
Violations found at inspection are grounds to deny the certificate
A temporary certificate of compliance may be issued for up to 30 days for minor violations, but not where conditions make the home uninhabitable or unsafe
In practice the borough points sellers to the Pine Hill Fire District smoke alarm, CO alarm and fire extinguisher inspection (see fire_cert)

fees.label: Continued certificate of occupancy (town code section 10-1.10b10(c))
Temporary certificate of occupancy, issuance or renewal (section 10-1.10b10(d))
fees.quote: The fee for the issuance and the renewal of a temporary certificate of occupancy $50.

resale_co.how_to_apply: The borough's Construction Office page says to contact the Pine Hill Fire Department at (856) 783-8666 to obtain a Certificate of Occupancy for the resale of a property. Confirm with the borough whether a separate Construction Office continued C.O. (town code fee $150) is also required, or whether the fire district certificate is the resale C.O. Construction Office paperwork can be dropped off and picked up daily 8:30 am to 4:00 pm; Construction Official James Gallagher, (856) 783-7400 x 208.

evidence.quote: To obtain a Certificate of Occupancy (C.O.) for the resale of a property, please contact the Pine Hill Fire Department: (856) 783-8666.

No person, group of persons, associations, partnerships or corporations, or any combination thereof, who own, manage, conduct or operate a dwelling unit shall sell, rent, lease, sublet or permit the same to be occupied or rented
without first securing from the Construction Official a certificate of occupancy or a continued certificate of occupancy for said dwelling unit.
Shall mean and include any conveyance or transfer of title, whether voluntary or involuntary, of real estate.
within five working days from the receipt of such application and the payment of the proper fees.
An application for a certificate of occupancy or continued certificate of occupancy shall be valid for six months from the date the application is filed.

All applications for the issuance of a certificate of occupancy or continued certificate of occupancy as well as any applications for reinspection of property for the issuance of a certificate of occupancy or continued certificate of occupancy shall be accompanied by the fee stated herein.

resale_co.notes: Changed from not_found: Pine Hill's town code, Chapter 10, section 10-1.10 (Certificates of Occupancy and Fees), read through the ecode360 print view, bars selling a dwelling unit without first getting a certificate of occupancy or continued certificate of occupancy from the Construction Official, and defines 'sale' as any transfer of title. The live borough Construction Office page, however, sends resale C.O. requests to the Pine Hill Fire Department (856-783-8666, which is also the fire district business office number), and the fire district's resale packet covers only smoke alarms, CO alarms and the fire extinguisher. So it is unclear whether the borough runs a separate Construction Office resale inspection with the $150 code fee, or treats the fire district certificate as the resale C.O.; confidence is medium until confirmed by phone. The code's reinspection sentence says reinspection requests must also be accompanied by the fee. Rentals are separate: rental units must be registered (section 10-1.10b13) and need a Certificate of Habitability through the Construction Office (Technical Assistant Lisa Kensil, 856-783-7400 x 202).

requirements: Power to the house must be on before scheduling, or an approved Special Circumstance form (extra fee, plus a follow-up inspection before anyone moves in)
Smoke alarm on every level within 15 feet of the bedrooms
Smoke alarms older than 10 years must be replaced before inspection
Hardwired smoke alarms must stay and cannot be replaced with battery alarms
CO alarm in the hallway within 10 feet of all bedroom doors; CO alarms older than 7 years must be replaced; not plugged into switched outlets or outlets against floor molding
Fire extinguisher rated 2A10BC (5 lbs), brand new or dated/tagged for the current year, mounted visibly within 10 feet of the kitchen or toward an exit from the kitchen (form still lists it)

authorities.name: Pine Hill Fire District #1, Bureau of Fire Prevention
authorities.area_served: Borough of Pine Hill (the LEA registry notes the former Pine Valley Borough was absorbed into Pine Hill; the district site does not say how it treats former Pine Valley addresses)
authorities.lead_time: More than 10 business days before the inspection date for the lowest fee; inspections are done one day a week. Form and payment must be received before an appointment is scheduled.

fees.label: More than 10 business days before inspection
fees.quote: More than 10 business days prior to inspection: $45.00

fees.label: 5 to 9 business days before inspection
fees.quote: 5 To 9 business days prior to inspection: $90.00

fees.label: 4 or less business days before inspection
fees.quote: 4 or less business days prior to inspection: $161.00

fees.label: Re-inspection
fees.quote: In the event that a re-inspection is required a fee of $20.00 shall be required

fees.label: Special Circumstance (power off with hardwired alarms): additional fee on top of the normal fee, same tiers, e.g. 10+ business days
fees.quote: Special Circumstance Fee Schedule: More than 10 business days prior to inspection: $45.00

fees.label: Penalty for occupying without the required follow-up inspection (Special Circumstance cases)
fees.quote: THE OCCUPANTS SHALL BE ISSUED A MINIMUM DAILY PENALTY OF $500.00, NOT TO EXCEED $5,000.00 PER DAY.

authorities.how_to_apply: Fill out the application in the Smoke Detector Inspection Packet and mail it or drop it off with a check or money order (no cash) at the Bureau of Fire Prevention, 1109 Erial Road, Pine Hill, NJ 08021. The form and payment must be received before an appointment is scheduled; the office then contacts you. If dropping off, put it in the mailbox and send a follow-up email. The office is part time and voicemail is not checked daily, so email firemarshal@pinehillfiredistrict.com for a faster reply. Fees are non-refundable.

fire_cert.notes: Pine Hill Fire District #1 is a separate fire district (Board of Fire Commissioners) at 1109 Erial Road. Fire Marshal Robert Fowler Jr.; Fire Inspector Nicholas Woods (inspector@pinehillfiredistrict.com). Office line 856-784-0030 goes to voicemail and is not checked daily; the district business office is 856-783-8666. The November 2025 packet still requires a fire extinguisher, which the state dropped from the sale certificate in February 2025 (P.L.2025, c.19), so confirm with the district. The NJ DCA fire directory lists a second smoke compliance phone, (856) 784-3993.

other_items.label: Rental registration and Certificate of Habitability (if the buyer will rent)
other_items.detail: Rental dwelling units must be registered with the borough, and a new owner of a registered rental must notify the borough within 10 days after receiving the deed; a Certificate of Habitability for rentals comes from the Construction Office.
